newsitem.title: USA: Merrill Lynch names Komansky CEO, chairman.
newsitem.headline: Merrill Lynch names Komansky CEO, chairman.

text.p: Merrill Lynch & Co. said Monday its chairman, Daniel Tully, will retire next year and be replaced by David Komansky, who is currently president and chief operating officer.
Komansky, 57, will take over as chairman on April 15 upon the retirement of Tully, who will turn 65 next year. In the interim Komansky will succeed Tully as chief executive officer on Dec. 28.
Tully has served as CEO since May 1992 and chairman since 1993. Merrill said its board of directors elected Komansky to the positions at its regular meeting Monday.
Komansky, who also will retain the positions of president and COO, had been considered the heir to the chairman's office since accepting those positions in 1995.
In a telephone interview, Komansky said he didn't anticipate making any strategic changes after taking the reins at the nation's largest brokerage.
"I'm most concerned with successfully carrying forward the strategies we've been following for some time now," he said."
Wall Street took the news in stride, with Merrill's shares falling 12.5 cents to $67.625 on the New York Stock Exchange.

Prior to becoming president and COO, Komansky was executive vice president, global debt and equity markets group, with executive management responsibility for debt and equity trading and institutional sales, on a global basis.
